title: Stocks end a short week with a big jump
text: Today was a half day: trading stopped at 1 p.m. Eastern time. In that short session, the S&P 500 fund (SPY) rose 1.6% and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) rose 2.7%. For the whole week, SPY is up about 5.6% and QQQ about 7%, after a rough drop the week before. Every stock and fund on our list went up today. The biggest gains came from Rocket Lab (up 8.2%), AMD (up 4.6%), Amazon (up 4.0%) and Broadcom (up 3.8%). Fewer people trade on holidays, so prices can move more than usual on days like this. Markets are closed this weekend and reopen Monday.

title: AI suppliers bounced harder, but are still far from their highs
text: The five AI supplier companies on our list (NVIDIA, Broadcom, TSMC, Vertiv and AMD) rose about 3.1% on average today. The four AI giants (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta) rose about 2.1%. Even so, the suppliers are still about 38% below their highest price of the past year, while the giants are about 19% below. The suppliers also have higher risk scores (about 6.7 out of 10, compared with 4.3 for the giants). Higher risk means bigger swings in both directions.

title: NVIDIA lagged the chip rally today
text: NVIDIA rose only 0.8% today, while AMD rose 4.6% and TSMC rose 3.2%. Over the whole week, though, NVIDIA is up about 20%, the most on our list. Next week is busy for the company: its CEO, Jensen Huang, is set to meet privately with House committees on December 1 and to speak at a public Senate hearing on December 3 about rules for selling chips to other countries. News from Washington can make the stock jump or drop quickly.

title: Interest rates are still high
text: The 10 year Treasury yield is the interest the U.S. government pays to borrow money for 10 years. It averaged 5.13% in October, up from 4.09% a year earlier. Many traders expect the Federal Reserve to raise its own rate at its December meeting. When safe bonds pay more, some investors are less willing to pay high prices for fast growing companies, which can hold those stocks back.

title: Cyber Monday is next
text: Monday, November 30, is Cyber Monday, usually the biggest online shopping day of the year. Adobe, which tracks online sales, forecasts about $15.1 billion of U.S. online spending that day, 6.2% more than last year. This is a forecast, not a final number. Strong shopping numbers can help companies like Amazon, and they also tell us how confident shoppers feel.

title: Lesson 71: Why one day does not make a trend
text: A trend is the general direction a price moves over weeks or months, not over one day. Today almost everything went up. Last week, almost everything went down. If you only looked at one day, you would get two opposite stories. Think of a basketball player: one great game does not make them a star, and one bad game does not make them a bad player. You look at the whole season. Investors do the same thing. They look at how a company does over many months and years: its sales, its profits and its price. Our 52 week range and the price history on this page help you see the bigger picture. A good habit: before you react to one big day, zoom out and ask, what has this stock done over the last year?

title: What this update covers
text: Prices are from today's close, Friday, November 27, a half day for U.S. markets. Risk scores and price scenarios use those prices. Analyst price targets are shown for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace; targets and some company numbers for Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical are not available on our free data plan. The 10 year yield is a monthly average through October. Weekly changes compare today's prices with last Friday's close. News comes from public reports, and we link to each source.
